messages.body_plain:
Hi Dirk,

upstream suspects that the issue to build r-cran-rstan might be connected to
the boost version that is used.

Its to late to change anything for bookworm but having r-cran-bh 1.81 in
experimental could help clarifying the issue with r-cran-rstan.

Kind regards
   Andreas.

Date: Tue, 07 Mar 2023 10:58:37 -0800
From: bgoodri <notifications at github.com>
To: stan-dev/rstan <rstan at noreply.github.com>
Cc: Andreas Tille <tille at debian.org>, Mention <mention at noreply.github.com>
Subject: Re: [stan-dev/rstan] Does not build on 32 bit architectures any more (Issue #1032)

If bookworm is going to use a version of Boost that is less than the BH 1.81 which is on CRAN, then you could get the previous version of r-cran-rstan under the freeze. In the version of rstan on CRAN, I just changed the compilation to deal with linker errors induced by Boost 1.81, but that apparently induced different errors on 32bit architectures. 

--

messages.body_plain:
On 3/8/23 12:48, Andreas Tille wrote:
> upstream suspects that the issue to build r-cran-rstan might be connected to
> the boost version that is used.

I've managed to get this building (along with passing autopkgtests) in an i386 chroot
with a patch. It probably should be able to build on other 32-bit archs too.

Changes pushed to salsa.

It took a bit of tussling with the Makevars file to get it right, because it
is impossible to tune some of the gcc/g++ based options that R passes, since it
is hard-coded in "/etc/R/Makeconf", which is a bit of a bummer.
(And no, I don't want to hear that this is how it is since time immemorial, every single
build system I've ever used has an option to tune compiler options, except this one)

@Andreas: Please do not upload the package, these changes might not be appropriate at freeze time.
And when you do the next upload, kindly do check if it builds without the 32-bit
patch (provided the situation with bh/boost settles down).

Thanks,
Nilesh

On 8 March 2023 at 14:18, Andreas Tille wrote:
| Am Wed, Mar 08, 2023 at 06:28:05AM -0600 schrieb Dirk Eddelbuettel:
| > 
| > As you may know, I am upstream for BH 1.81.0-1. It reached CRAN after a month
| > of careful alignment with reverse depende on Jan 22.  That is six weeks ago.
| > I cannot do anything about you deciding not to update it sooner, sorry.  
| 
| $ apt showsrc r-cran-bh | grep -e ^Version -e Maintainer
| Version: 1.74.0-2
| Maintainer: Dirk Eddelbuettel <edd at debian.org>

But that package is an 'empty shell' so that we do not need the 120mb package
BH from CRAN?

   edd@rob:~/deb/bh(master)$ cat debian/control 
   Source: r-cran-bh
   Section: gnu-r
   Priority: optional
   Maintainer: Dirk Eddelbuettel <edd at debian.org>
   Build-Depends: debhelper-compat (= 11), r-base-dev (>= 4.1.1), dh-r
   Standards-Version: 4.6.0
   Vcs-Browser: https://salsa.debian.org/edd/r-cran-bh
   Vcs-Git: https://salsa.debian.org/edd/r-cran-bh.git
   Homepage: https://cran.r-project.org/package=BH
   
   Package: r-cran-bh
   Architecture: all
   Multi-Arch: foreign
   Depends: ${misc:Depends}, libboost-dev (>= 1.74.0)
   Description: (Virtual) GNU R package to provide BH
    The CRAN package BH provides a (large) subset of Boost.  This package tricks
    R into believing BH is installed when we just depend on the distribution's
    Boost packages.  The actual set of Boost libraries could get fine-tuned. In
    short, we avoid doubling up the 140+ mb of the 'BH' package which are alredy
    in libboost-dev.
   edd@rob:~/deb/bh(master)$ 

In short, it has little to do with BH at CRAN (and we both once thought that
was a good idea) and depends only Debian's Boost packages. I have no control
over their release cycle. It is as we both know a pretty big package.

Dirk

-- 
dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org
